18e22a5cf14b7e4e7d9f7ac1bbdd2bd27e5a8a4b.summary: Threatpost article (2020) on Android/SpyC32.A, a new variant of spyware from threat group APT-C-23 (also called Two-Tailed Scorpion and Desert Scorpion), as reported from ESET research. Used in active campaigns against victims in the Middle East. Disguised as a WeMessage messaging app on Google Play. Extends surveillance to WhatsApp and Telegram, hides calls behind a blank overlay, dismisses security-app notifications, and hides its C2, which can be changed remotely. Earlier versions were distributed through a fake 'DigitalApps' store. Users are advised to install apps only from official…

180e190a6e08372a2688b571644dadb584a364e2.summary: FireEye's report covers FIN7, a financially motivated criminal group it has tracked since 2015. U.S. prosecutors unsealed indictments and announced arrests of three leadership members on Aug. 1, 2018. The group mainly stole payment card data, pivoted to finance departments when card data was encrypted, and sent spear phishing lures to many sectors. It used the CARBANAK backdoor, digitally signed its malware, and operated partly through a front company, Combi Security, which recruited unwitting staff. The report also links later campaigns (BATELEUR, GRIFFON, BIRDDOG) to FIN7 with varying…

1893329c4ced716898038e57e624618a6b4f9857.summary: Blog post from FireEye's Advanced Practices team introducing SCANdalous, an automated system that uses third-party network scan data to find threat actor command-and-control infrastructure before it is used against clients. It recounts case studies on APT39, APT34, APT33, FIN6, FIN7 and UNC1878, and reports metrics: over five thousand signatures, over two million hits, and 21.7% of analyst-marked IP addresses found earlier by the system.
